direct_claims: This chart is about the annual reductions in carbon dioxide emissions required under different mitigation start dates to keep global temperature rise below 1.5°C.
It belongs to the climate change and emissions policy domain.
The chart was published by Our World in Data.
The subtitle states that the scenarios are based on the CO2 reductions necessary if mitigation had started, with global emissions peaking and then quickly reducing, in the given year.
The title and subtitle indicate that these pathways are tied to a carbon-budget framing for limiting warming to 1.5°C.
The note states that the carbon budgets are based on a greater than 66% chance of staying below 1.5°C from the IPCC's SR15 report.
The values are shown in billions of tonnes of CO2, which is a standard unit for comparing global annual emissions.
The source line cites Robbie Andrew (2019) as the data source.
The note ties the scenario framing to the IPCC Special Report on 1.5°C.
